3I/ATLAS: a 3D solar-wind reconstruction

', f'

Author: Codex-root with Codex observation, external-model and solver sub-agents. Generated {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}.

', f'

{stage} The reference run {esc(best)} gives PN-good-time-weighted proton density {f(v["n"])} cm⁻³, heliocentric speed {f(v["v"])} km/s, and incident proton flux {f(v["f_incident"])} cm⁻² s⁻¹. These are model-dependent estimates, not measurements at the comet.

', '

Full numerical convergence is not established. Changing the combined GLM/Rusanov dissipation treatment changes the wider 96×16×96-grid PN-weighted incident flux by about 37%, with pointwise differences up to 47%. That common-CFL test is closely related to the historical wide_fine reference but is not a calibrated ±37% uncertainty or a confidence interval. Earlier narrow-grid tests also showed substantial method dependence. This issue is separate from boundary-input uncertainty and successful fixed-method grid tests. The requested demonstration that further numerical changes cannot materially alter the answer has therefore not yet been met.

', '

Time-series chart · Numerical time series · Top-down animation · Stream-contrast animation · Machine-readable results · Reproduction guide

', '', '

Epoch, frame and incident flux

', '

The published pointing sequence spans 2025-12-03 12:37:38 to 2025-12-04 17:22:29 UTC. The existing analysis_06 bounds, 12:04:07 to 10:11:54 the next day, describe retained frame metadata rather than accepted science exposure. The 45 accepted PN intervals instead begin at 13:04:03.002 and end at 09:56:03.002, totaling 21,362.284 s. All quoted exposure-weighted means integrate the model over these exact intervals. GTIs and original FITS paths; evidence report.

', '

The mesh uses the fixed solar equator and the ascending node on the J2000 ecliptic as longitude zero. Full geometric JPL Horizons vectors use UTC explicitly. Carrington maps rotate at 14.1844° per day; their phase is anchored by GONG sub-Earth longitude and the actual Earth vector. The independent IAU phase differs by only 0.169°, while per-map phase residuals reach 0.731°. WSA map orientation was checked against the original magnetogram (correlation 0.9855); treating the generic DU documentation as the exact GONG pixel origin would be incorrect here. Independent phase audit; pixel check.

', '

The ordinary heliocentric flux is F=nₚ|vSW|. The physically incident flux used in the final flux chart is Fincident=nₚ|vSW−vcomet|. The comet moves outward at about 43 km/s radially and 66 km/s in total, so the distinction is several percent to approximately 10%. Both fluxes and both speeds are retained in the CSV. No spacecraft was treated as being co-located with the comet.

', '

Inputs and physical closure

', '

The solar input is 25 actual daily WSA 5.4 maps, driven by GONGZ photospheric magnetograms, from November 10 through December 4. WSA supplies radial field and empirical speed at 21.5 solar radii (0.099985 AU). Its coronal calculation uses PFSS and a Schatten current-sheet extension; this project implements the heliospheric MHD stage, rather than rebuilding that upstream coronal model. Official WSA model description; retrieval URLs and hashes.

', f'

Pre-epoch STEREO-A and Solar Orbiter measurements over November 10–24 set instrument-balanced density, magnetic and thermal normalizations. Wind is entirely held out. The calibrated boundary uses n₄₀₀={f(m["density_1au_at400_cm3"])} cm⁻³ at 1 AU, T₄₀₀={f(m["proton_temperature_01au_at400_K"])} K at the inner boundary, and a WSA field multiplier {f(m["WSA_Br_multiplier"])}. At native map nodes, constant momentum flux sets n∝v⁻² and constant thermal pressure sets T∝v². Independent linear interpolation of these primitive fields does not exactly preserve those nonlinear relations between nodes; that boundary-interpolation assumption is audited separately. Pressure is 2nₚkBTₚ, assuming equal electron and proton temperatures and hydrogen-only mass density. The chosen WSA-to-MHD speed reduction is 50 km/s; it is tested as an uncertain model choice, not represented as the exact ENLIL boundary transformation.

', '

STEREO-A is only about 1.1° away from the comet in solar latitude; Solar Orbiter is about 15.9° away. Their training density-normalization medians differ substantially (6.05 versus 11.25 cm⁻³), motivating separate low/high-density experiments. Spacecraft normalization does not recover the neutral coma, heavy-ion charge states or a unique unobserved density map. A prior heavy-ion fraction 3×10⁻⁴–10⁻…197 tokens truncated…nsing research; independent primary-catalogue audit.

', '

Numerical implementation and tests

', '

The C++17 solver evolves mass, three Cartesian momentum components, total energy, three magnetic components and a GLM cleaning variable in all three spatial directions. Exact integrated spherical face-area vectors handle geometry; MC-limited MUSCL reconstruction, a Rusanov flux and SSPRK2 advance the solution. Solar gravity is included. The main closure γ=1.5 represents effective distributed heating; γ=5/3 is a sensitivity experiment, not an exact reproduction of ENLIL’s explicit heating. Radial boundaries are imposed wind/outflow, longitude is periodic, and latitude boundaries extrapolate spherical components. Rejected high-order steps use a recorded first-order fallback; no hidden density or pressure floors are used. Solver equations and implementation.

', '

The production shell reaches 2.3 AU. Low-resolution experiments preceded refinements. Both ±30° and ±60° latitude domains were tested because radial superfast flow does not remove transverse causal communication. At the inner boundary the characteristic fast speed is a substantial fraction of radial speed, so a narrow angular wedge requires an explicit domain test.

', f'

Uniform Cartesian MHD is preserved to float-output precision. The cold radial mass-flux errors decrease 1.235% → 0.331% → 0.104%. The Brio–Wu shock tube keeps normal field exactly constant and density L1 error against a 1600-cell reference decreases 0.01358 → 0.005794 at 400 → 800 cells. Synthetic fast/slow streams develop nonradial flow while remaining positive. These verify numerical behavior; self-comparison against a fine reference does not constitute an independent exact MHD Riemann solution. Test metrics; Canonical Brio–Wu definition.

', '

An independent 8192-cell Athena++ HLLD/characteristic-PPM/RK3 reference was also built and frozen. Baseline density L1 errors against it fall 0.02529 → 0.01899 → 0.01382 → 0.006954 at 400 → 800 → 1600 → 6400 cells. A separate check against published exact plateau states retains a nonmonotonic left-state mismatch and the known intermediate/compound-wave branch caveat. This adds independent verification without treating a nonunique Riemann branch as a unique exact target. Pinned Athena reference and reproduction; published-state comparison; author manuscript.

', '

A second independent Athena++ benchmark propagates the actual rotating boundary with B=0, using HLLC/PLM/RK2, the same gravity and thermal closure, and exactly prescribed inner mass flux. Positivity floors are configured to abort rather than conceal failures; none activate. Its 72→96-cell refinement changes the PN-weighted incident flux by −10.47% and the local time series by up to about 24.5%. The in-house hydrodynamic LLF controls also retain substantial method dependence. Thus the outstanding transport sensitivity exists without magnetic cleaning. A smooth hot radial-wind check against the analytic Bernoulli relation gives coarse speed errors of approximately −2.47% for the in-house solver and −0.35% for Athena; these checks do not identify a major pressure-unit or gravity error. Inputs, problem generator, native outputs and comparisons.

', '

A separate CUDA float64 implementation keeps the same finite-volume equations and both LLF flux variants. Fused multiply-add is disabled for a close CPU comparison. Five small cases, including evolving electric fields and the scaled outer boundary, give identical saved float32 fields and probe values at output precision. A full 25-day coarse global run also reproduces all 5,925 steps, 236 first-order fallbacks, divergence statistics and saved probe values; its GPU solve takes about 11 s versus 60 s on one CPU thread. These are implementation-agreement checks, not independent physical validation. CUDA implementation and reproduction; all agreement evidence.

', '

The single-precision CUDA branch is separately checked against double precision. On the complete 25-day 96×16×96 global run, maximum incident-flux differences during the pointing are 0.0095%, and the PN mean changes less; the same step and fallback counts are retained. Its solve takes about 97 s versus 244 s in double precision, with 78 versus 156 MB of device arrays. Full coarse split and cone cases also keep precision effects well below the numerical-method discrepancy. The optimized branch changes host/device synchronization only and reproduces saved FP32 fields, probes and rejection statistics exactly in full coarse global, split and CME cases. Measured 96-grid flux kernels take less than 0.25 ms in double precision and less than 0.04 ms in single precision. These timings are subject to shared-device load. Full wide precision check; kernel-duration measurements.

', '

Refinement, domain and additional-physics checks

', f'

Criteria were recorded before reviewing production refinements: maximum pointwise differences ≤10% for density and flux, ≤5% for speed; halving the timestep should change each by ≤1%. Current Boolean results: {esc(statuses)}. These tests cover the complete published interval. A pass establishes adequate resolution only for the chosen macroscopic inputs and numerical method.

', table(['Comparison','Max density Δ','Max speed Δ','Max heliocentric flux Δ'],comparisonrows), '

Latitude-width experiments must be interpreted separately from cell-resolution experiments. The early coarse ±30°/±60° comparison changes flux by approximately 14%; that is measured sensitivity, not a validated ±14% uncertainty bound. Comparisons of different numerical fluxes also need to remain separate from domain comparisons. Exact-GLM preprocessing with the original dissipation changes the coarse PN flux by less than 1%, whereas a split GLM treatment with lower transverse dissipation can change it much more. This numerical-method dependence must not be hidden behind a single successful refinement test. Full divergence and scheme diagnostics; independent domain assessment.

', '

GLM cleaning leaves nonzero magnetic divergence. In the narrow-domain final day-34 snapshots, the comet-neighborhood h|div B|/|B| decreases from about 0.018 on the coarse grid to 0.006 on the medium grid, and the medium nearest-cell value is about 0.003. These are not PN-epoch measurements or diagnostics of the wider fine reference. A monopole-force scale is small relative to bulk inertia, but that ratio is not a rigorous accumulated-flux error bound. These calculations do not establish a converged magnetic topology. Controls below quantify changing B, temperature, speed, density and γ; their grid sizes are recorded individually and their spread is not an uncertainty percentile.

', '

The wider fine run uses CFL 0.4 versus 0.35 in the wider medium run, so that comparison combines spatial and Courant-number refinement. The separate narrow-domain timestep test contextualizes this difference without proving that its effect is identical in the wider domain. No extrapolation is allowed in the interval comparisons, and exact interval endpoints are included.

', '

The accelerated refinement series uses a common CFL of 0.35, ±60° latitude and the scaled outer magnetic boundary. Each flux-method pair differs only in the documented numerical flux. Initial 96×16×96 runs reproduce the historical angular aspect ratio. Latitude-only refinement to 96×32×96 changes local incident flux by 16% with global LLF and 53% with split LLF, despite a much smaller change in the global-LLF PN mean. This confirms that the earlier two-grid pass was insufficient. Balanced angular refinements use 96×32×96, 144×48×144 and 192×64×192 when completed, reaching 1.875° spacing in both angles. Induction, timestep and domain controls are separately named.

', table(['Accelerated comparison','Max density Δ','Max speed Δ','Max incident flux Δ'],acceleratedrows), '

A physical boundary audit distinguishes pure rotation from independently evolving daily magnetic maps. With zero azimuthal velocity and source_surface_au=0, a frozen Carrington radial-field pattern is compatible with the imposed Parker tangential field. Daily changes require an additional inductive boundary electric field omitted from the original production model. Frozen-field controls preserve daily speed, density and temperature while holding one observed magnetic map fixed. Optional inductive controls solve a full-sphere surface Poisson problem for a minimal electric correction after removing a small net-flux component (about 0.112% of field RMS). The extra electric field is piecewise constant over each map interval, while the physical maps interpolate linearly. It changes tangential magnetic stresses and is an additional closure, not a uniquely measured electric field.

', '

The Poisson correction cancels the map evolution to approximately 10⁻¹² relative residual using its native staggered face fields. The present solver instead interpolates cell-centred electric columns, leaving roughly 29–31% of the original map-evolution residual; it does not implement constrained transport or exact boundary cancellation. Separate outer-boundary controls extrapolate Br∝r⁻² and Bt∝r⁻¹ instead of copying B, because GLM waves can carry an outer divergence error inward even through superfast wind. The zero-electric-field parser control exactly reproduces the original coarse probe output. These experiments isolate boundary effects from changes in numerical flux. Equations, tests and representation limits; controlled CPU implementation.
